objective: In this workspace, `src/relay/workspace/julius-tools/node-tool-adapter.ts` builds the paths its search tools emit with `path.relative`, which uses the HOST separator. On Windows that breaks the tools outright: `search.find` and `search.glob` filter with `file.includes(needle)`, so a needle written the ordinary way — `src/relay` — matches NOTHING in a workspace full of matching files, and a Coding Agent told there is no such file believes it; and `search.grep` emits `path:line:text` whose path half changes shape by host, so anything reading it back is host-dependent. Make the SPELLING of every path these three tools emit host-independent, and make the needle match a path spelled either way. Introduce two pure exported helpers — `juliusSearchPath(relativePath)` and `juliusSearchNeedleMatches(relativePath, needle)` — use them in all three search cases, and change nothing else about what the tools may read or where they may look. `seed/src/relay/workspace/julius-tools/node-tool-search-paths.test.ts` is already written and currently fails, on Linux as well as Windows, because it exercises the helpers with backslash input directly. The file to edit exists and is tracked by git — edit it in place.
requirements: Export a pure function `juliusSearchPath(relativePath: string): string` that returns the same workspace-relative path with every separator as `/`, on every host. It normalises SEPARATORS and nothing else: no trimming, no case change, no resolution, no removal of dots or spaces, and an empty string stays empty.

Export a pure function `juliusSearchNeedleMatches(relativePath: string, needle: string): boolean` that decides a match without the separator spelling of either side mattering: a needle written with `/` must match a path spelled with `\`, and the reverse. Keep the existing behaviours exactly — a `*` is stripped as it is today, an empty needle still matches everything, and a needle that does not occur still does not match. The fix must stop the separator deciding a match; it must not widen what matches.

Use `juliusSearchPath` for every path `search.grep`, `search.find` and `search.glob` emit, and `juliusSearchNeedleMatches` for the `search.find`/`search.glob` filter. A helper that exists and is not called is not a fix.
`search.grep` keeps emitting `path:line:text`: only the path half changes shape. The line number and the matched text are untouched, and the 1000-match and `maxFiles` bounds are unchanged.

CONTAINMENT IS UNCHANGED. No path outside the workspace root becomes reachable or emitted: no absolute path, no `..` prefix, no drive-qualified path. A change that normalised its way out of the workspace would be a containment failure wearing a formatting fix.
Touch no other tool case. `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `fs.remove`, `fs.copy`, `fs.move`, `process.exec` and the policy, evidence and mutation bookkeeping are outside this mission.
PURITY. Both helpers are free of side effects, read no clock, no environment and no filesystem, and mutate no argument. The same input answers the same way.

This is TypeScript run by Node's own type stripping. Use only erasable syntax: no `enum`, no `namespace`, no parameter properties in a constructor, and no new import from outside the file's existing set.
After your edits `node --import ./.julius/loader.mjs --test src/relay/workspace/julius-tools/node-tool-search-paths.test.ts` must exit zero, with no network access and no third-party dependency.
constraints: Edit `src/relay/workspace/julius-tools/node-tool-adapter.ts` in place. You have `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep` and `Edit`; you cannot create files or run commands, and you do not need to.
Do not edit `src/relay/workspace/julius-tools/node-tool-search-paths.test.ts`. It is the specification you are implementing against, not part of the deliverable.
Add no dependency and no import from outside this workspace: the sandbox that runs the test has no network access and no `node_modules`.
Do not reformat the file. It is written in a deliberately dense style; match it. A whitespace-only rewrite of 63 lines would bury the change this mission is judged on.
Do not weaken any existing guarantee to make the test pass: the workspace bound, the `maxFiles` walk limit, the 1000-match cap and the evidence the tool records all stay as they are.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `juliusSearchPath` is exported, pure, and returns a POSIX-separated path for backslash, forward-slash and mixed input on every host, normalising separators and nothing else.

`juliusSearchNeedleMatches` is exported and matches a needle against a path without the separator spelling of either side mattering, while keeping the `*` stripping, the empty-needle behaviour and the non-match behaviour exactly as they are today.
All three search cases in the adapter use the helpers: every path `search.grep`, `search.find` and `search.glob` emits is POSIX-separated, and the find/glob filter goes through the needle matcher.
`search.grep` still emits `path:line:text` with the line number and matched text unchanged.
No absolute, `..`-prefixed or drive-qualified path is emitted, and the workspace bound, the `maxFiles` walk limit and the 1000-match cap are unchanged.
No other tool case, and no policy, evidence or mutation bookkeeping, is changed; the file is not reformatted.
